name: Silverstein
label: Victory
lede: Five kids from Burlington, Ontario named themselves after the man who wrote children's poems, taught their singer to scream, and made four screamo records for Victory that still get sung back word for word.

eras.title: A punk kid learns to scream
eras.text: Silverstein started in Burlington, Ontario in 2000 as a side project for Shane Told, then 19 and still in the punk band Jerk Circus. Guitarist Josh Bradford wanted a screamer, so Told taught himself, and by late 2002 Victory Records had signed them.

years.h: Silverstein forms in Burlington, named after Shel Silverstein
years.p: Shane Told starts the band as a side project at 19 and names it after the children's author Shel Silverstein.
years.xp: Told was in his first year at the University of Guelph, studying music, genetics and molecular biology. His main band was the punk group Jerk Circus, which rehearsed in his parents' basement and broke up at the end of 2002.

years.h: Summer's Stellar Gaze: Silverstein's self-released first EP
years.p: Silverstein self-releases its first EP, Summer's Stellar Gaze, six months after forming.

years.h: Billy Hamilton finds Silverstein on an Ontario message board
years.p: Billy Hamilton reads that Silverstein needs a bassist on an Ontario music message board and joins in December 2000.

years.h: Richard McWalter leaves to study engineering. Neil Boshart joins
years.p: Original guitarist Richard McWalter moves to Victoria, British Columbia to study engineering. Neil Boshart takes over lead guitar.

years.h: Shane Told learns to scream, sometimes loud enough to bring police
years.p: Josh Bradford wanted a screamer, so Shane Told taught himself, partly at Warped Tour contests. The result is the 2002 EP When the Shadows Beam.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Told practiced in remote spots so he wouldn't bother his housemates, and the noise occasionally drew police attention.

years.h: Silverstein signs to Victory Records
years.p: With Boshart, Bradford, Hamilton, Koehler and Told in place, Silverstein signs to Chicago's Victory Records in October 2002.

eras.title: Smashed Into Pieces
eras.text: Silverstein's first album was made in five weeks in southern Ontario and sold far past anyone's expectations. Shane Told dropped out of university a month before it came out.

years.h: Shane Told drops out of the University of Guelph
years.p: Shane Told leaves his music, genetics and molecular biology studies at Guelph in April 2003, weeks before Silverstein's debut. The first two songs, Smashed Into Pieces and Giving Up, go online April 3 and 5.

years.cap: When Broken Is Easily Fixed, Victory Records, 2003
years.src: Wikipedia: When Broken Is Easily Fixed · Wikipedia: Silverstein
years.h: When Broken Is Easily Fixed: Silverstein's Victory debut
years.p: Recorded January and February 2003 with Justin Koop at Mount Fairview and Unity Gain. It sold 179,000 copies by June 2007, per Wikipedia's album page.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's band page says the album sold over 200,000 copies. Alternative Press called it one of the most personal and creative albums of 2003.

Ten years to the day after release, the band put out a re-recorded Smashed Into Pieces.

years.h: When Broken Is Easily Fixed reissued with a DVD
years.p: Victory reissues Silverstein's debut with bonus tracks and a DVD of live footage and band interviews.

eras.title: A tantrum, a hit and a Juno
eras.text: Discovering the Waterfront put Silverstein in the Billboard Top 40 and on Warped Tour. The song Shane Told didn't want on it became one of the band's anthems.

years.h: Discovering the Waterfront debuts at No. 34
years.p: Made with Cameron Webb at Capitol Studios in Hollywood, it sells 26,229 copies its first week and over 100,000 in the US by year's end.
years.xp: Sales reached 232,000 by June 2007, and the band said 400,000 by the tenth anniversary. Music Canada certified it Gold on September 5, 2024.

years.h: Shane Told breaks studio gear over My Heroine
years.p: Shane Told didn't want My Heroine on Discovering the Waterfront because the demo sounded bad, and started breaking things in the studio. Victory Records covered the cost.
years.xp: My Heroine got a video anyway, alongside Smile in Your Sleep and the title track. Loudwire later called My Heroine and Discovering the Waterfront classic anthems of the 2000s screamo movement.

years.h: Warped Tour, Taste of Chaos, Never Sleep Again
years.p: Silverstein spends 2005 and 2006 on the Vans Warped Tour, the Never Sleep Again Tour and Taste of Chaos.

years.h: Silverstein loses the Juno for Best New Band to [[Bedouin Soundclash|e0036453-ce34-4095-af40-8c70ee07cef1]]
years.p: Silverstein is nominated for the 2006 Juno Award for New Group of the Year, three years after its debut, and loses to Bedouin Soundclash.

years.h: An American Idol hopeful screams Smashed Into Pieces
years.p: A contestant named Ryan Heart auditions for American Idol with Silverstein's Smashed Into Pieces, inhale screams included. Alternative Press reported the judges weren't impressed.

years.h: Arrivals & Departures tops the indie chart
years.p: Produced by Mark Trombino, it debuts at No. 25 on the Billboard 200 with about 27,000 sold. Shane Told later called it the band's worst record.
years.xp: The band went for a stripped-down rock sound with little layering, and some fans balked. Told explained in a 2018 interview that it wasn't a slick record.
play: If You Could See into My Soul

eras.title: A shipwreck, then goodbye to Victory
eras.text: Silverstein's fourth album was a four-chapter concept record about a mutiny, and it finished the band's four-album Victory contract. A year later they were on Hopeless.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Shipwreck in the Sand · Wikipedia: Silverstein
years.h: A Shipwreck in the Sand: a mutiny in four chapters
years.p: A crew turns on its captain when no land appears; Shane Told called it a metaphor for betrayal. Liam Cormier of [[Cancer Bats|00b952be-6c97-4880-84f9-06de584b491b]], Scott Wade of [[Comeback Kid|6d152109-c447-446d-9a06-3621c920bebd]] and Lights guest. No. 33 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp: Cameron Webb came back to produce at Metalworks in Mississauga because the band was unhappy with the sound of Arrivals & Departures. The album was announced through a viral marketing campaign, and was the last of Silverstein's four Victory albums.

years.h: The Decade Tour gets a live DVD
years.p: Silverstein marks ten years with the Decade Tour and a live DVD released June 8, 2010.

years.h: Silverstein leaves Victory Records for Hopeless
years.p: With the contract done, Silverstein leaves Victory in 2010 and signs to Hopeless Records.

eras.title: Twenty-five years of noise
eras.text: Silverstein never broke up. The band lost a guitarist after 11 years, moved to UNFD, picked up two more Juno nominations and kept touring its Victory records to crowds who grew up on them.

years.h: Rescue: Silverstein's first album on Hopeless
years.p: Silverstein's fifth album and first after Victory Records.

years.h: Short Songs: 22 tracks, none over 90 seconds
years.p: Half of the EP is covers of punk songs, all under a minute and a half.

years.h: Neil Boshart leaves after 11 years. Paul Marc Rousseau joins
years.p: Lead guitarist Neil Boshart leaves Silverstein. Paul Marc Rousseau, formerly of I Am Committing a Sin, replaces him.

years.h: A world tour for Discovering the Waterfront at ten
years.p: Silverstein tours the world playing its 2005 album for its tenth anniversary.

years.cap: When Broken Is Easily Fixed at 15
years.h: Silverstein takes When Broken Is Easily Fixed on the road at 15
years.p: The band's 2003 debut gets its own 15-year anniversary tour across 2018 and 2019.

years.h: A Beautiful Place to Drown gets a Juno nod
years.p: Silverstein's first album on UNFD, the label it joined in 2019, is nominated for Rock Album of the Year at the 2021 Junos.

years.h: Antibloom and Pink Moon, and 25 Years of Noise
years.p: Silverstein releases a two-album set, Antibloom on February 21 and Pink Moon on September 19, and tours as 25 Years of Noise. Antibloom is nominated for a 2026 Juno.
